title: Cleaning and Damage Fees Level Placement Standard
content:
This standard governs the fee level at which a Cleaning and Damage Fees report is held.

## Clauses in force

1. Each level covers the incidents its level definition, its affected extent, its offline assumption, its professional-cleaning requirement and its odor-treatment flag describe (its typical incidents are examples), and only the incident categories listed in its entry gate.
2. When the evidence matches a lower level than the one reported, the reviewer moves the report down, and never up. Reviewers may move a report to a different level when the evidence shows one; the direction is down only.
3. The conditions never charged — muddy footprints, rain or snow water, loose crumbs under one spot, normal wear and tear, and service animal shedding — are not chargeable at any level, and a report consisting only of them is denied (non-chargeable condition).

## Retired clause

The clause "A report is held at the lowest level whose definition matches the evidence on file" is **no longer in force**. It has been superseded by the current basis for level moves on cleaning fee reports and is kept here only so that it is not read as current law.

## Points of judgement

| Situation | Judgement under the clauses in force |
|---|---|
| The evidence matches a higher level than the one reported | The level is not moved up |
| The evidence matches a lower level than the one reported | The reviewer moves the report down |
| The report shows only rain water and muddy footprints | Denied as a non-chargeable condition |
| The report shows a soda spill together with muddy footprints | The footprints are not chargeable; the spill is placed at the level its descriptors and entry gate allow |
| The incident category reported is not listed in a level's entry gate | That level does not cover the incident |

superseded_clauses: A report is held at the lowest level whose definition matches the evidence on file
